tencentMissingNote: Tencent's 271-episode upload is the Taiwan dub. It skips EP038 (never aired outside Japan) and EP065 (not aired in Taiwan), so Tencent numbers run 1 behind from EP039 and 2 behind from EP066. Verified by matching Tencent cover frames for 35-39, 45, 62-66, 74, 81.

1: Where it all begins: a late-sleeping 10-year-old in Pallet Town ends up with a starter that wants nothing to do with him. Sets the heart of the whole series.
2: A desperate dash to the Viridian City Pokémon Center, and the first run-in with the trio who will turn up in nearly every episode after.
3: Ash catches his first Pokémon, a Caterpie, in Viridian Forest to Misty's horror; it evolves into Metapod while protecting him from Team Rocket.
4: Samurai, a young trainer, challenges Ash in Viridian Forest. A Beedrill swarm carries off Metapod, which evolves into Butterfree during the rescue.
5: Ash's first Gym battle, against Brock's Rock types, and a lesson that a bad matchup isn't won by stubbornness alone.
6: On Mt. Moon, a scientist named Seymour protects the Clefairy and their Moon Stone from Team Rocket. Cute but forgettable.
7: Misty's three older sisters run the Cerulean Gym. Misty battles Ash herself, and Team Rocket's interruption hands Ash the Cascade Badge.
8: Ash meets A.J., an undefeated trainer whose Sandshrew is raised with a brutal training regime, and starts to wonder how hard is too hard.
9: Pokémon Tech, a cram school for rich kids, lets students skip the badge journey. Ash defends a bullied student and takes on top student Giselle. Skippable.
10: A hidden village where a girl named Melanie nurses abandoned Pokémon, guarded by a fiercely protective Bulbasaur.
11: A Charmander waits on a rock for the trainer who promised to come back, even as the rain starts. One of the series' defining emotional episodes.
12: A gang of sunglasses-wearing Squirtle terrorizes a town with pranks, and their leader turns out to have a story.
13: Bill, a researcher stuck in a Kabuto costume, waits at his lighthouse for a giant mystery Pokémon, until Team Rocket scares it away.
14: Lt. Surge's Raichu humiliates Pikachu, and Pikachu has to decide what kind of Pokémon it wants to be.
15: Free cruise tickets on the St. Anne turn out to be a Team Rocket scam to steal trainers' Pokémon. James gets conned into buying a Magikarp.
16: Trapped inside the capsized St. Anne, Ash's group and Team Rocket must work together to escape; James's Magikarp finally gets useful.
17: Separated on an island of 'giant Pokémon', Ash's and Team Rocket's Pokémon team up. The giants are robots in a Team Rocket theme park.
18: Misty enters a beach beauty contest against Jessie and a cross-dressing James to pay off a broken boat. Pure filler; shelved in the US for years.
19: A giant Tentacruel attacks Porta Vista after a hotel developer wrecks the coral reef. Heavy-handed environmental message.
20: A ghost story at a seaside festival: a woman waiting forever for her lost love, and Brock falls hard for her. Atmospheric and a bit spooky.
21: Butterfree season arrives on the coast, and Ash faces a hard choice. Bring tissues.
22: Ash challenges Saffron City's Sabrina, a cold Psychic-type leader with unsettling powers, and loses badly. First of a three-part arc.
23: To stand a chance against Sabrina, Ash heads to Lavender Town's haunted Pokémon Tower. The series' most famous spooky episode.
24: The Sabrina arc's payoff: a ghost with a sense of humor against a psychic with none.
25: A Mankey steals Ash's hat and evolves into a rampaging Primeape; Ash eventually catches it.
26: Ash insults perfume in front of Erika and gets banned from the Celadon Gym; he sneaks in, Team Rocket sets it on fire, and he earns the Rainbow Badge.
27: A Hypno meant to cure adults' insomnia leaves the town's kids thinking they're Pokémon. Odd and skippable.
28: A breeder named Suzie entrusts her Vulpix to Brock after a Pokémon fashion contest. Brock fans only.
29: Ash enters Primeape in the P1 Grand Prix fighting tournament, then leaves it with a fighter who can train it better.
30: A city plagued by power outages: Magnemite flock to sick Pikachu, and the culprit in the power plant is a Grimer and a Muk, which Ash catches.
31: Trainers are hired to drive Diglett away from a dam site, but the Diglett are defending their home. Ekans and Koffing evolve.
32: A ninja mansion full of trap doors: Ash takes on Koga's Fuchsia Gym and wins the Soul Badge.
33: Ash rides an injured girl's Ponyta in a ranch race that Team Rocket has rigged; Ponyta evolves into Rapidash mid-race.
34: A Tarzan story in the Safari Zone: a boy raised by Kangaskhan is reunited with his parents.
35: A Safari Zone catching contest against Team Rocket, a warden with a secret, and rumors of a legendary dragon. Never dubbed in English (it has a gun scene), but the Taiwan dub on Tencent includes it.
36: Carrying medicine across the Cycling Road, the group clashes with a bike gang that Team Rocket has teamed up with.
37: Duplica, an impersonator whose Ditto can transform into anything except its face, battles Team Rocket. Light and fun.
38: Ash is digitized into the Pokémon transfer system to stop Team Rocket. Its flashing scene caused the 1997 'Pokémon Shock' seizures and it was never re-aired. Not on Tencent; history only, photosensitivity warning.
39: Pikachu wanders into a forest full of wild Pikachu, and Ash has to think about what's best for his friend.
40: A boy's three older brothers each evolved their Eevee and pressure him to do the same; he decides Eevee is fine as it is.
41: A sleeping Snorlax blocks a town's water supply, and everyone tries to wake it. Not the Snorlax Ash later catches.
42: Two rival gyms in lawless Dark City fight for official recognition and try to drag Ash into it.
43: A struggling magician and his Exeggutor cause chaos in town; Charmander evolves into a Charmeleon that no longer respects Ash.
44: A shopkeeper wants her weak Paras to evolve for its mushroom medicine; Charmeleon's disobedience continues.
45: Meet Jigglypuff, a frustrated singer whose audience keeps falling asleep. Starts a running gag that lasts years.
46: A dig site awakens Pokémon nobody has seen in millennia, and Ash's fire Pokémon is pushed to its limit.
47: Pikachu chokes on an apple, but the Pokémon Center is full after a Team Rocket accident, so an ordinary doctor and his Chansey step in.
48: James goes home to a family fortune and the arranged marriage he ran away from. Hilarious, and quietly sweet.
49: A Farfetch'd steals Misty's Poké Balls, and the gang track down its trainer.
50: The egg Ash found hatches into Togepi; Ash and Misty argue over who keeps it and Team Rocket try to steal it.
51: Bulbasaur is drawn to a hidden garden where its kind gather, and has to decide about its future.
52: Misty and Jessie compete in the Princess Festival tournament for dolls they both wanted as kids.
53: On Kids' Day a boy wants to meet the Meowth that once saved him, and Team Rocket's Meowth pretends to be it.
54: Ash trains alongside Officer Jenny's Growlithe police squad; Team Rocket fakes Jenny's voice to command them.
55: Todd, a Pokémon photographer, is hired by Team Rocket to 'capture' Pikachu and takes it literally. Introduces Todd.
56: Short on badges, Ash takes the Pokémon League entrance exam and finds out how little textbook knowledge he has.
57: Misty leaves Psyduck at a breeding center run by Butch and Cassidy, Team Rocket's rival duo, who frame Ash's group.
58: Cinnabar Island's Gym Leader hides behind riddles and disguises, and Team Rocket has taken over his gym.
59: Ash's Blaine rematch inside a volcano: the episode many fans call the league run's best battle.
60: A sleeping Blastoise king on an island; Squirtle revives its Squad persona to find out why it won't wake.
61: The Cerulean Gym is in trouble, and Misty battles Team Rocket in a water show while dressed as a mermaid.
62: Clefairy steal machine parts in Viridian City to build a spaceship. The season's weakest episode on IMDb.
63: The last badge, and the identity of Viridian City's Gym Leader.
64: Ash's mom takes in a runaway Mr. Mime from a circus, and Ash dresses up as a Mr. Mime to fill in.
65: The group helps a lost Jynx get home to Santa before Christmas. Not on Tencent (not aired in Taiwan), and later withdrawn in the US over Jynx’s design.
66: A blizzard separates Ash from everyone, leaving him and his Pokémon to get through the night together.
67: Back in Pallet Town, Ash finds Gary waiting, and Professor Oak has something to say to them both before the League.
68: On Seafoam Island, Professor Oak and Ash study how Slowpoke evolves into Slowbro, and Jessie tries to force it.
69: A surfer and his blue-eyed Pikachu, Puka, chase a legendary wave, and Pikachu learns to surf.
70: Bulbasaur gets paralyzed by Gloom's scent in a big greenhouse. Short and skippable.
71: Psyduck lands a role in an all-Pokémon movie opposite a prima-donna Wigglytuff.
72: Meowth's backstory: how a street cat taught itself to walk and talk like a human, and why. Team Rocket's best episode.
73: Ash trains in the mountains with Elite Four member Bruno, who mostly makes them do chores; a giant Onix rampages.
74: The group uncovers the ancient city of Pokémopolis, waking a giant Gengar and Alakazam. Kaiju-style oddity.
75: Ash helps Mandi, a League-bound trainer, get his stolen badges back from Team Rocket.
76: The Indigo Plateau opening ceremony: Ash joins the torch relay and meets the field before the League begins.
77: The Indigo League begins, starting with a water field that suits some of Ash's team better than others.
78: Rounds two and three of the League, on the rock and ice fields.
79: The fourth round, and Ash's toughest opponent yet.
80: Ash meets Ritchie, a trainer who seems a lot like him, Pikachu included.
81: A promise between rivals, and a battle that defines how Ash's first League run is remembered.
82: Ash's first League run ends, and he has to figure out what it meant.

extras.title: Pokémon Red & Green launch (Japan)
extras.summary: Game Boy release that started everything. The anime adapts this Kanto region a year later.

extras.title: Pokémon Blue launch (Japan)
extras.summary: Revised Japanese version; its code became the base of the international Red & Blue.

extras.title: "Pokémon Shock": anime pulled off air
extras.summary: EP038's flashing scene sent hundreds of viewers to hospital. The show went on a four-month hiatus and returned with EP039 on 1998-04-16.

extras.title: Mewtwo Strikes Back (Pokémon: The First Movie)
extras.summary: A cloned Pokémon with a grudge invites the world’s strongest trainers to an island fortress. The franchise’s most famous film; best watched after EP063.

extras.title: Pikachu's Vacation (short)
extras.summary: A 20-minute short that played before the first movie: Ash’s Pokémon spend a day at a Pokémon-only resort. For young kids. Not in Tencent’s movie collection.

extras.title: Pokémon Stadium launch (Japan, N64)
extras.summary: First home-console battle game, letting players see their Game Boy Pokémon in 3D.

extras.title: Pokémon Yellow launch (Japan)
extras.titleZh: 《宝可梦 皮卡丘》日本发售
extras.summary: Remake built around the anime: you start with a Pikachu that follows you and won't go in its Poké Ball, and meet Jessie & James.

extras.title: Pokémon Red & Blue launch (North America)
extras.summary: The games hit the US weeks after the English dub started airing, and the worldwide craze took off.
